newsitem.title: USA: Santa Fe pipeline leg seen shut through Sat.
newsitem.headline: Santa Fe pipeline leg seen shut through Sat.

text.p: A leg of the Santa Fe Pacific Pipeline into Reno, Nevada, will remain shut at least through Saturday, a company official said, as workers investigate a probable leak in the 50,000 barrel-per-day line.
"I don't have much hope for the line to be back in service before Saturday or Sunday," said John Abboud, senior vice president of operations and engineering at Santa Fe Pacific Pipeline Partners LP.
Over the weekend, the company shut the 120-mile segment of line which carries diesel fuel, jet fuel, and gasoline from Roseville, California, outside Sacramento, to Reno, Nevada.
The shutdown occurred after officials received reports of a petroleum odor and oil sheen in a creek in California's Sierra Nevada mountains.
The mountainous terrain and thick snow could keep investigators from reopening the line until the weekend, Abboud said.
Meanwhile, large San Francisco refiners, which include Tosco Corp , Unocal Corp , and Exxon Corp, have been advised to truck products to customers affected by the shutdown.
